northStar: Find a calm shared-chat interface where many people can understand one agent's attention and queue.
constraint: Pure frontend; the agent returns Ok for every turn.
falsifiable: A participant can identify active work, next work, and their own queue position within five seconds.

proven.claim: All 20 policies render and complete every seeded request without duplicate responses.
Observed peak active work matches sequential, bounded, and unbounded Effect concurrency.

unproven.claim: People can understand and trust each strategy without knowing its implementation.
The good-for and tradeoff labels predict how each policy feels in a real shared room.

disproven.claim: A persistent queue sidebar is necessary to make agent attention visible.

openQuestions: Do people prefer continuously refilled lanes or explicit batch barriers?
Is role priority or identity rotation perceived as fairer in facilitated rooms?
When does motion clarify concurrency, and when does it become noise?
Should superseded requests remain visible or collapse into the newest request?
